01.note: MEASURED: CUDA is 2.32x faster than CPU for pose (70.4 -> 30.4 ms/frame) on a GTX 1080, and agrees to within 0.94px across 6150 keypoints (worst conf delta 8e-6) - sub-pixel but NOT bit-identical. Three false results came first, all the same shape - CUDA silently falling back to CPU while the benchmark reported the non-difference: (1) the installed onnxruntime was the CPU-only build, so device='cpu' was not even the binding constraint; (2) onnxruntime-gpu 1.28 wants CUDA 13 on a CUDA 12.6 machine - it ADVERTISED the provider, failed to create it, and reported 0.98x; (3) pose_device()'s forced-device branch returned before the torch import that registers the CUDA DLLs, so the one caller that forces cuda (the benchmark) was the one that skipped enabling it - 1.00x. Each reads as 'the GPU does not help', which would have chosen the production worker host off CPU-vs-CPU. The durable fix is that posebench.py now asks the REAL session get_providers() and refuses to time a fallback. Analyzer suite green: 123 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Two latent bugs fixed en route: contract.py computed parents[3] at IMPORT time (crashed any monorepo-less install before the documented SWINGSAGE_SCHEMA_DIR override could apply) and test_contract.py had the same walk. Gates: local 141/2s/1x; docker build clean; IN-CONTAINER suite 103/13s/1x exit 0 - the from-scratch reproducibility proof. Club-head best.pt remains a local-only asset with no fetch path (open, later step).

04.note: The queue loop is BUILT AND PROVEN locally, host-agnostically: dispatch (lib/jobs/dispatch.ts, behind JOBS_DRIVER=queue - opt-in, spawn stays default) -> QStash local dev server -> worker HTTP server (service/server.py, signature-verified, single-flight) -> source download -> pipeline.run with throttled event forwarding -> artifact PUTs -> verified done callback -> Postgres job state and view flip. E2E harness (pnpm --filter web queue:e2e) PASSED on pro_2: job done, view ready at revision 2, fps 60. The worker holds no DB/storage credential - only URLs plus an HMAC-signed per-job token whose claims carry {jobId, viewId, actorId, targetRevision, exp}; internal routes (/api/internal/jobs/*) verify it and write as the enqueuing user (no elevation on a request path, D26). Failure taxonomy is load-bearing: PipelineError acks 200 (refusals are answers, never retried); infra failures 5xx into QStash's retry schedule. done is verified, not believed (isPublished at targetRevision before the row flips). WORKER_CLUB_DETECTOR must be explicit (path or 'none') - the standing club-detector trap, now enforced at enqueue. Gates: analyzer 165/2s/1x (+24 new); web tsc+lint clean, vitest 179; schema additive (Job.runner) locked, 100 passed; container rebuilt with qstash 3.4.0 pin, in-container 127/13s/1x. Deploy + production QStash credentials + fair queuing/retry/DLQ are later steps; worker host stays the OPEN handoff row.

05.note: Fair queuing, dead letters, orphan detection, backpressure, capacity model - all host-agnostic, all proven live against the QStash dev server. Publish now carries flowControl (key user-<id>, JOBS_FLOW_PARALLELISM, default 1 - keys allow no colon, dev server enforces) and a failureCallback (/api/internal/jobs/<id>/failure) that authenticates via the job token recovered from the dead message's OWN body (sourceBody - the dev server does send it), settles job+view failed, writes jobs.error (its first writer) and logs the dlqId. Events route stamps jobs.last_event_at (migration 0011) on every worker post; reconcile()'s new queue branch settles running rows silent past JOBS_QUEUE_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_S (900) and queued rows past JOBS_QUEUE_PENDING_TIMEOUT_S (3600). Enqueue refuses at JOBS_MAX_ACTIVE_PER_USER (3) active jobs, counted by swing-ownership join not RLS visibility. done events self-report elapsedS into the job log. All policy is pure + unit-tested in lib/jobs/policy.ts (13 tests). PROVEN LIVE: positive e2e PASSED twice (view rev 3->4->5; 'pipeline elapsed 407.3s' in the log), negative path PASSED for real - worker killed, QStash burned 4 deliveries (~35min backoff), failure callback settled the job with dlqId 1787064288255-0. Gates: analyzer 165/2s/1x; web tsc+lint clean, vitest 192 (+13); migration applied. Capacity model in docs/decisions/platform-data.md: ~4.5-6.8min/job CPU pose (269-407s measured), ~10.5 jobs/hr/worker single-flight; CUDA projects ~4.5min - p95<180s SLO needs a faster host class and/or horizontal workers. route-auth meta-test now accepts jobContextForClaims (the shared verifier) alongside requireJobAccess.

06.note: Every model asset the pipeline loads now has a committed sha256 and a stated source (service/models.py), and a container that cannot get one refuses to start. Four assets: MediaPipe landmarker + RTMW wholebody + RTMPose body from public URLs, and the PRIVATE club-head best.pt from SWINGSAGE_CLUB_WEIGHTS_URL - published through the media store the web app already owns (pnpm --filter web models:publish -> swing-models bucket, CONTENT-ADDRESSED key, prints hash + signed URL), so D26 holds: the worker still has no storage credential. Hash is verified on the temp file BEFORE the atomic rename, so a partial download can never become the loaded model; server.py runs the same check before binding; entrypoint.sh bootstraps then execs (SWINGSAGE_SKIP_MODEL_BOOTSTRAP=1 for the in-image test suite). Closed the step-03 open item (best.pt had no fetch path) and added the worker-side half of the never-default-the-club-detector rule: a stated-but-absent detector is now a SpecError at spec parse, not a failure after five minutes of pose.
